title: 1 May 1947 — Where Rights Meet Their Boundaries
summary: The Assembly debates inter-State trade, forced labour and compulsory service, child labour, religious freedom, conversion of minors, and minority cultural and educational rights.

title: Forced Labour vs Compulsory Public Service
summary: A prohibition on trafficking, begar and involuntary servitude is remitted after the House confronts whether broad language might also prohibit conscription or compulsory public service.

title: Freedom of Religion and Social Reform
summary: Conscience, profession, practice and propagation of religion are debated alongside public order, secular activity, social reform and access to religious institutions.

title: Conversion of Minors — Rights, Family and Coercion
summary: The House struggles to reconcile coercion and fraud concerns with parental authority, family unity and a minor's conscience, ultimately sending the clause back for reconsideration.

title: Minority Cultural and Educational Rights
summary: Language, script, culture, admission to State institutions and minority educational institutions become the next frontier of the rights debate.
